name: Easy Baked Cinnamon-Sugar Biscuit "Doughnut Holes" (Cooking with Kids)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe contains steps that can be done by smaller hands! You know your child (and their cooking abilities) best, so get them involved where you feel comfortable. Have fun!
Preheat oven to 350°F. Coat two large baking sheets with cooking spray.
Open biscuit tube, separate biscuits, then cut each into quarters. Have fun rolling the biscuit dough into balls, then divide between the baking sheets, spacing at least 1 inch apart.
Place baking sheets in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until "doughnut holes" are golden and cooked through, 15-20 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, place sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl, stir to combine, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup granulated sugar
1 tbsp cinnamon, ground

instructions.primary_message: Place butter in a small saucepan and melt over medium heat. Transfer to a large bowl.

When the doughnut holes are done, carefully add to the bowl with the butter and stir to coat. Transfer buttered doughnut holes to several lunch-sized paper bags. Add a portion of the cinnamon sugar to each, roll the edges to seal the bag, and shake well to coat. (Alternatively, the sugar can be added to the bowl with the buttered doughnut holes, tossing to coat.)
Arrange doughnut holes on a platter (or eat straight out of the bag!), share, and enjoy!
